target: Hon somnar direkt.
english: She falls asleep right away.
old: Swedish present tense is the same for all persons: `jag talar`, `du talar`, `han talar`. The verb form never changes by person. Easy compared to most European languages.
focus: Anchor on 'somnar': Swedish uses one verb form for every subject – hon somnar, jag somnar, du somnar – unlike English's 3rd-person -s. No backticks.

target: Vi njöt av solnedgången.
english: We enjoyed the sunset.
old: Swedish glues "the" onto the end of the noun. hund (a dog) → hunden (the dog). hus (a house) → huset (the house). No separate word.
focus: Anchor on 'solnedgången': Swedish tacks 'the' onto the noun's end (solnedgång to solnedgången = the sunset). Drop the hund/hus filler.

target: De pratar svenska hemma.
english: They speak Swedish at home.
old: 'Prata' → 'pratar' (talk/chat): Group 1, more informal than 'tala'.
focus: Register: prata is the everyday word for 'talk/chat'; tala sounds more formal. Quote pratar; drop the group-1 conjugation framing.

target: Butiken öppnar klockan tio.
english: The store opens at ten.
old: Two genders – common (suffix -n) and neuter (suffix -t). bilen (the car, common) vs huset (the house, neuter). The ending reveals the gender.
focus: Anchor on 'butiken': two genders – common nouns take -en (butiken = the shop), neuter take -et (huset). Drop the abstract bilen/huset table framing.

target: Han jobbar på ett sjukhus.
english: He works at a hospital.
old: 'Jobba' → 'jobbar' (work): Group 1 verb (-ar ending). 'Arbeta' → 'arbetar' is more formal.
focus: Register: jobba is casual 'work', arbeta is more formal. Quote jobbar; drop the group-1 conjugation label.

target: Vi äter frukost klockan halv åtta.
english: We eat breakfast at half past seven.
old: "Halv åtta" = 7:30 (half TO eight). "Frukost" = breakfast.
focus: Time trap: halv atta = 7:30, not 8:30 – Swedish counts to the next hour (half TO eight). Quote halv atta; drop the frukost gloss.

target: Vi äter middag klockan sex.
english: We eat dinner at six o'clock.
old: "Middag" = dinner (evening meal). Lunch is the midday meal.
focus: False-friend: middag looks like 'midday' but means dinner, the evening meal. Quote middag; drop the lunch aside.

target: Jag vill lära mig mer svenska.
english: I want to learn more Swedish.
old: 'Vill' (want) – modal verbs in Swedish don't change form: 'jag vill', 'du vill', 'han vill'.
focus: False-friend: vill means 'want', not English 'will'. Quote vill; keep it to that one point.

target: I Sverige äter man ofta middag vid sex.
english: In Sweden one often eats dinner at six.
old: Swedish is V2: the verb is always the second element. `Idag äter jag pizza` (today I eat pizza), not `idag jag äter`. Subject jumps after the verb.
focus: V2 word order: fronting 'I Sverige' pushes the verb ahead of the subject – I Sverige ater man (in Sweden eats one). Remove backticks; anchor on this card's own inversion.

target: Du skämtar väl inte med mig om det här?
english: You are surely not joking with me about this?
old: Subordinating conjunctions don't push the verb to the very end (that's German). But they DO flip the inte/verb order. Main: `verb + inte`. Sub: `inte + verb`.
focus: Strip the backticks. Anchor on this main clause: 'du skämtar inte' = verb + inte. State the real trap: in a subordinate clause (att-, om-, som-) it flips to inte + verb, unlike English which never moves 'not'.

target: Det är varmt ute.
english: It is warm outside.
old: `Det är` doesn't care about gender or number of what follows: `det är en bok`, `det är böcker`. Always `det är` in front, regardless.
focus: Strip the backticks. Keep the point: dummy subject stays 'det är' regardless of the gender/number of what follows – learners wrongly reach for 'den är' with en-words. Quote 'Det är varmt'.

target: Det finns bröd på hyllan.
english: There is bread on the shelf.
old: `det är` = 'it is / there is'. `Det finns` = 'there is/are' for existence. `Det är en bil` (it is a car) vs `det finns en bil` (there is a car).
focus: Contrast det är (it is) vs det finns (there is/exists), anchored to 'Det finns bröd pa hyllan'; strip backticks; one contrast only.

target: Hittills har allt gått bra.
english: So far everything has gone well.
old: Perfect tense uses `har + supinum`: `jag har talat`, `vi har sett`. The supinum is the form ending -at / -t / -tt / -it – distinct from past tense.
focus: Perfect = har + supinum, anchored to 'har allt gatt'; note supinum (gatt) differs from the past-tense form; strip backticks; trim the table.

target: God kväll, hoppas du har haft en bra dag.
english: Good evening, I hope you've had a good day.
old: 'Bra' (good) never changes form – it's the same in all positions. Comparative: 'bättre', superlative: 'bäst'.
focus: 'Bra' never inflects, unlike stor/stort - anchor to 'en bra dag'; one rule only, drop the comparative list.

target: Året då allt förändrades.
english: The year when everything changed.
old: The V2 rule doesn't apply in subordinate clauses (after att, som, när, etc.) – there the subject comes before the verb.
focus: Anchor to 'da allt forandrades': in a subordinate clause the subject stays before the verb (no V2); plain words.

target: Hur vi löser problemet vet jag inte.
english: How we solve the problem I don't know.
old: Fronted indirect question as topic: "Hur vi löser" + inverted main: "vet jag inte."
focus: Anchor to the card: the whole clause 'Hur vi loser problemet' fills the first slot, so the main verb inverts - 'vet jag inte'; plain words, no jargon.

target: Hur gammal är du?
english: How old are you?
old: Swedish only has one 'you' in modern use: `du`. Use it with strangers, your boss, the king – everyone. The formal `Ni` is essentially extinct outside very formal letters.
focus: Modern Swedish uses 'du' for everyone; strip backticks; anchor to 'du'; keep it to the one du-universal point.

target: I princip är vi överens.
english: In principle, we agree.
old: If anything but the subject opens the sentence, the subject inverts after the verb – V2 rule. `Idag äter jag pizza` (today eat I pizza). Same rule as German/Dutch.
focus: Anchor to 'I princip ar vi': a non-subject first element forces verb-second, subject third; keep the German/Dutch parallel; strip backticks.

target: Min familj bor i en liten stad i södern.
english: My family lives in a small town in the south.
old: 'Liten' is highly irregular: en→liten, ett→litet, definite→lilla, plural→små.
focus: liten is suppletive — its definite/plural forms look nothing like it; quote 'en liten stad', note the plural is 'små'. Drop the full paradigm table.

target: Skynda dig så att vi inte missar bussen dit!
english: Hurry up so we don't miss the bus!
old: In subordinate clauses, `inte` moves before the verb: `att jag inte äter pizza` (that I don't eat pizza). Compare to the main-clause order `jag äter inte pizza`.
focus: Strip backticks. Anchor to the card's 'så att vi inte missar' — in a subordinate clause inte comes before the verb.

target: Snart kommer sommaren under sommaren till slut.
english: Soon summer will come during the summer in the end.
old: "Snart" = soon. Fronted adverb triggers V2 inversion.
focus: Lead with the inversion, not the gloss; quote 'Snart kommer sommaren' — a fronted adverb pushes the verb ahead of the subject.

target: Det kan inte stämma.
english: That can't be right.
old: `inte` (not) goes after the verb in main clauses: `jag äter inte pizza` (I don't eat pizza). Watch the position – putting `inte` first is wrong.
focus: Strip backticks. Anchor to 'Det kan inte stämma' — in a main clause inte follows the verb.

target: Sex, sju, åtta, nio, tio.
english: Six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
old: "Sju" (7) contains the tricky sj-sound [ɧ]. "Åtta" has double-t making the å short.
focus: One rule only — keep the sju [ɧ] sj-sound note (the hardest Swedish sound), drop the åtta clause. Quote 'sju'.

target: Hon undrade var vi bodde.
english: She wondered where we lived.
old: Reported questions with wh-words keep the question word: var, när, hur, etc.
focus: Highlight the word-order trap — a reported wh-question keeps subject before verb: 'var vi bodde', not 'var bodde vi'.

target: Vad synd att du inte kunde komma med oss idag!
english: What a shame that you could not come with us today!
old: After att, när, om, eftersom: inte (not) goes before the verb. Jag vet att han inte kommer (I know that he isn't coming).
focus: Strip the generic example; anchor to the card's 'att du inte kunde komma' — after att, inte sits before the verb.

target: De vackra blommorna doftar gott.
english: The beautiful flowers smell nice.
old: "Dofta" = smell (emit scent). "Gott" (neuter) here because it's an adverb, not adjective.
focus: Drop the dofta gloss; focus on why 'gott' takes neuter -t after the verb (it's an adverb, not an adjective). Quote 'doftar gott'.

target: Skit samma, vi gör det på vårt sätt istället.
english: Whatever, we will do it our way instead.
old: Mildly vulgar but extremely common in casual Swedish.
focus: Quote 'Skit samma'; note it's a crude/slangy 'whatever', casual speech only.

target: Det var som fan efter jobbet egentligen!
english: That was unbelievable after work actually!
old: Mildly vulgar exclamation expressing astonishment.
focus: Quote 'som fan'; note it's a vulgar intensifier (roughly 'as hell'), casual/vulgar register only.

target: Skorstensfejarens uniform var svart av sot och aska.
english: The chimney sweep's uniform was black from soot and ash.
old: Swedish loves compound nouns – long words made of smaller ones. `Tandborste` = tooth + brush. Break them apart to read: `tand` + `borste`. The last piece carries the gender.
focus: Anchor on the card's own compound Skorstensfejarens (skorsten + fejare = chimney sweeper); drop backticks and the Tandborste example; last piece sets the gender.

target: Hon kan prata tre språk.
english: She can speak three languages.
old: "Kan" means both 'can' and 'know how to.' No 'att' before the infinitive after modals.
focus: Keep only kan = can AND know how to, anchored on Hon kan prata (she knows how to speak); drop the generic no-att clause.

target: Vi vet inte var han bor med familjen.
english: We don't know where he lives with the family.
old: In subordinate clauses after "var/att/om": subject + inte + verb.
focus: Sentence has no inte in its subclause; retarget to the real phenomenon: after var the subclause keeps subject-verb order (var han bor, not var bor han).

target: Jag vill ha en öl.
english: I want a beer.
old: Direct "jag vill ha" is casual but common among friends.
focus: Make the register stake explicit: jag vill ha en öl is blunt for ordering; kan jag få en öl is politer. Quote vill ha from the card.

target: Kan jag betala med kort under sommaren?
english: Can I pay by card during the summer?
old: "Kort" = card. Sweden is nearly cashless – cards accepted everywhere.
focus: Drop the kort = card gloss; keep the genuine note that Sweden is nearly cashless so card pays everywhere. Quote kort/betala med kort.

target: Kanske kommer han imorgon.
english: Maybe he will come tomorrow.
old: "Inte" goes after the verb in main clauses: "Jag förstår inte" = I don't understand.
focus: Sentence has no inte; retarget to the real feature: kanske triggers V2 inversion (Kanske kommer han = maybe comes he), verb before subject.

target: Jag kan inte simma.
english: I can't swim.
old: "Kan inte" = can't. Negation always after the modal verb in main clauses.
focus: Drop the 'can't' re-translation; hook the rule that inte follows the finite/modal verb in main clauses – quote 'kan inte simma'.

target: Jag tycker inte om det.
english: I don't like it.
old: "Tycker inte om" = don't like. "Inte" splits "tycker" and "om" (particle).
focus: Lead with the surprise that inte splits the particle verb tycka...om: 'tycker inte om' – the om belongs to the verb, not a preposition.

target: Hur vill du betala just nu snart?
english: How do you want to pay right now soon?
old: Swedish dropped formal `you` in the 1960s-70s (`du-reformen`). Unlike French/German/Russian, there is no formal pronoun – `du` works for everyone.
focus: Strip the backticks (plain text). Keep the point: Swedish scrapped formal 'you' in the du-reform, so 'du' works for everyone – quote 'du'.

target: Det är alltid roligt att lära känna nya människor här.
english: It is always fun to get to know new people here.
old: 'Alltid' (always) – goes after the verb in main clauses: 'Jag äter alltid frukost'.
focus: Drop the 'always' gloss lead; hook that a frequency adverb sits right after the verb in main clauses – quote 'är alltid roligt'.

target: Jag har alltid älskat svensk natur nu.
english: I have always loved Swedish nature.
old: "Älska" → "älskat" (Group 1 supine: -at). Time adverbs go between har and supine.
focus: One rule only: cut the supine-formation half; keep that a time/frequency adverb goes between har and the supine – quote 'har alltid älskat'.

target: Redan klockan sex vaknade jag ibland också.
english: Sometimes I even woke up as early as six o'clock.
old: "Redan" = already. When fronted, V2 rule applies.
focus: Drop the 'already' gloss lead; hook that fronting anything forces the verb before the subject – quote 'Redan klockan sex vaknade jag'.

target: Huset är stort som vi såg i den gamla butiken igår.
english: The house is as big as the one we saw in the old shop yesterday.
old: Simple definite: "Huset" = the house. Suffix -et for ett-words.
focus: Hook the English trap: Swedish glues 'the' onto the noun as a suffix -et – 'huset' = the house, no separate article.

target: Dessutom regnar det.
english: Moreover, it's raining.
old: "Dessutom" = moreover. Sentence adverb – triggers V2.
focus: Drop the 'moreover' gloss lead; hook that a fronted sentence adverb forces verb-second – quote 'Dessutom regnar det'.

target: Vi hoppas att vädret blir bra verkligen.
english: We really hope the weather will be nice.
old: "Hoppas" is a deponent verb (s-form but active meaning). It takes an att-clause.
focus: De-jargon 'deponent': hoppas ends in -s so it looks passive, but it means active 'we hope' – quote 'hoppas'.

target: I och med att han slutade fick hon jobbet.
english: Since he quit, she got the job.
old: "I och med att" = since/given that.
focus: Hook the literal breakdown: 'i och med att' reads word-for-word as 'in and with that' but means given/since that. Quote the phrase.

target: Maten lagas av kocken.
english: The food is cooked by the chef.
old: S-passive is more common than bli-passive for habitual/general statements.
focus: Anchor to 'lagas': s-passive (verb + -s) beats bli-passive for habitual/general statements. Quote maten lagas av kocken.

target: Platsen dit vi reste på kvällen förra året.
english: The place we traveled to in the evening last year.
old: "Dit" = to where. "Platsen dit" = the place to which.
focus: Make it the dit-vs-där trap: 'dit' = to-where (motion), 'där' = where (static). Quote 'platsen dit'.
